goal: Ruler, laws and heirs: lead a nation, enact and repeal laws, and see what happens when the ruler dies.

findings.title: Ruler death (and so succession) cannot be reached in a play session: hunger is the only death and takes ~25,000 ticks
findings.detail: The goal asks to see what happens when the ruler dies. The player only dies of hunger: energy drains 100 per in-game day (30,000 ticks), starting at 85. In 6,156 ticks energy went 85 -> 64.7. There is no combat, hazard or other death. Even at full speed (50 tps) a death takes over 8 real minutes of standing still; on this machine (4-10 tps) it would have taken ~50 min, so the Succession screen ('THE RULE PASSES ON') was never seen. Expected: some way for a ruler to die or abdicate within a reasonable session, or a faster test path.
findings.repro: pt start --profile beyond-nations --game-dir /root/bn-wt-playtest064 --seed 106; space; Start; Begin; N; pt wait ... ; pt state (energy falls ~0.0033/tick)

findings.title: Nobody can be recruited as an heir: pawns out-walk the player and need 'Loyal' before R works
findings.detail: Succession needs a member pawn, but recruiting one is very hard early. Pawns wander as fast as the player walks: 6 walkto attempts between ticks 600 and 4,400 mostly ended 'stuck: not getting closer' at 20-50 m. The two pawns I reached were no use. Frank Brown led his own nation already. Charlotte Taylor said 'I'm loyal to Southham.' (needs Loyal). Three 10-coin gifts only moved her from Stranger to Acquaintance before she walked out of reach. Within 6,000 ticks NPCs had founded 9 nations and taken in most pawns. My nation stayed at 1 member, so any death would have ended the run.
findings.repro: pt start ... --seed 106; create nation (N); pt walkto pawn 60 (repeat); pt key r; pt key g

findings.title: Laws tab hides the fourth law (Rationing) at 960x540: no scroll and the row is cut
findings.detail: The Laws tab shows Taxes, Conscription and Borders. The game defines a fourth law, Rationing (Laws.All). LawsPanel.draw stops adding rows when the next block would not fit above the footer, and the tab has no scroll (the Nations tab does have Up/Down). So at this window size Rationing cannot be seen or enacted. Expected: every law can be reached, by scrolling or a more compact layout.
findings.repro: pt start ... --seed 106; N; O; click Laws (543,45); look below Borders

findings.title: No screen shows the heir or line of succession while you rule
findings.detail: Nations tab says 'Your nation: Northburg, 1 member, no settlement. You lead it.' Neither the Laws tab, Player Info nor the Controls screen says who would succeed you, or warns that with no heir your death ends the run. The player can't plan for succession or see that they need to recruit. Expected: an 'Heir: <name>' or 'No heir: your death ends the line' line in the Nations tab or Player Info.
findings.repro: pt start ... ; N; O (Nations tab); check Player Info panel

findings.title: Law countdown says 30 s but a repeal took 36.6 s to come into force
findings.detail: Laws proclaimed at tick 452 came into force at tick 2000 (31 s). The repeal proclaimed at 4172 came in at 6000 (36.6 s), while the panel said 'Off in 30 s'. Changes seem to land on 1000-tick law rounds, so the promised time is a lower bound and not exact.
findings.repro: O; Laws; click Conscription Off and Borders Closed; pt events (Statecraft chronicle entries)

findings.title: Simulation ran at 3.5-10 tps (of 50) and 1-4 fps through the whole session
findings.detail: pt status/state showed tps 3.5-10.3 and fps 1-4 the whole time. The machine was shared with other sessions, but it made every timed mechanic (30 s laws, hunger) take 5-10x longer in real time.

findings.title: Pawn name label is cut off at the right screen edge
findings.detail: With Frank Brown right beside the player, his floating label ran off the right edge: only 'Frank Br / Ambitio / (looking' showed. Expected the label to be clamped on screen.
findings.repro: walk up beside a pawn (pt walkto pawn) and screenshot

verdict: Enacting and repealing laws is clear and satisfying: the panel explains each effect in a line, shows the pending change with a countdown, and the chronicle announces it when it comes into force. The heir side of the goal can't be reached in a session. Hunger is the only way to die and takes most of an in-game day, recruiting anyone to be an heir means chasing pawns that out-walk you and earning their Loyalty, and nothing on screen tells you who your heir is. Rationing is also hidden off the bottom of the Laws tab.
